supporting_observations.claim: The periodic HTTPS connections align with the inventory-approved PixelForge updater: process 5684 ran from the approved path and made proxy connections to updates.pixelforge-suite.com at roughly five-minute intervals. One attempt received HTTP 407; later attempts succeeded.

A Dropbox updater executable ran as SYSTEM from a Dropbox Update path, although Dropbox is not among the approved services. The records show a DNS lookup for x7k9m2.akamaized.net shortly after it ran, but do not establish that the updater made that lookup or connected to the resolved address.

FILE-NWD-01 initiated an RPC connection to WS-LMARTINS-01. The inventory describes workstation patching as initiated from WS-SOKAFOR-01, so this connection does not match the stated patching practice; the records do not identify its purpose.

The domain controller recorded sam.okafor authentication associated with WS-LMARTINS-01, and WS-SOKAFOR-01 recorded a network logon for sam.okafor from that workstation. This is unusual given the stated practice that remote administration is performed from WS-SOKAFOR-01, but these records do not establish the authentication's purpose or whether it was authorized.
Other observed HTTPS proxy activity includes a successful Stack Overflow tunnel and a successful static.akamai.net tunnel; these records alone do not establish harmful activity.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records show CONNECT destinations, status, byte counts, and duration, but not the contents of the encrypted TLS sessions.
The Dropbox updater's execution and the later DNS lookup are observed, but the available records do not attribute that lookup or any network connection to the updater.
The supplied records do not establish the purpose or authorization of the FILE-NWD-01 RPC connection or the sam.okafor authentication.
claims_not_established: Whether the Dropbox updater or any other unapproved software transferred files or communicated with an external service.
Whether the FILE-NWD-01-initiated RPC connection was authorized maintenance, another legitimate activity, or malicious remote administration.
Whether sam.okafor's credentials were intentionally used or misused, and what activity followed the recorded authentication.
Whether any of the observed activity caused compromise, data access, or exfiltration.
additional_evidence_needed: Review FILE-NWD-01 logs and process telemetry around 13:31 UTC to determine what initiated the RPC connection and what actions occurred on WS-LMARTINS-01.
Verify with sam.okafor whether the 13:26 authentication from WS-LMARTINS-01 was expected; review corresponding authentication and session activity on both workstations.
Inspect WS-LMARTINS-01 for Dropbox installation, service configuration, persistence, file activity, and network telemetry attributable to DropboxUpdate.exe.
Obtain TLS inspection, endpoint process-to-network attribution, or equivalent telemetry for the relevant proxy sessions, if available.
